description: The India Water Resources Information System is a public portal launched by the Ministry of Jal Shakti under the National Hydrology Project, first in July 2019 and in a new version on 6 August 2020, that gathers water resources information into dashboards. These cover rainfall, river water levels and discharge, water bodies, groundwater levels, reservoir storages, evapotranspiration and soil moisture, with modules on water resources projects, data availability and tools for editing GIS layers. It receives data regularly from agencies including the Central Water Commission, Central Ground Water Board, India Meteorological Department, National Remote Sensing Centre and several states, drawing on the Water Information Management System where agencies enter manual and telemetry readings received by GPRS or satellite. Coverage: national, with state coverage growing. Access: free public portal; the licence and download formats are not stated in the release. Caveats: the page is a launch press release, so current layers and update cadence were not verified. It supports reservoir, flood and water availability analysis and emergency planning, and relates to the Murray-Darling Basin water information and Korean national water supply records in the catalogue.
